title: Codex-turn-to-generation map: bound per session (or retain while its rows run) so other sessions cannot evict a long id-less run's turn
outcome: A late, tagged, id-less Codex end of a long run, such as a 30+ minute full gate, still resolves its turn while other sessions start many commands. Entries are dropped when their session is removed. A test covers eviction.
acceptance: A late Codex end of an id-less command, tagged with the Codex turn it ran in, still ends that turn's host-observed test-run row with its own exit after other sessions have started commands in more than 256 Codex turns since it started; a test drives this through the shared app-server path.

The Codex-turn-to-TermAl-generation mapping is bounded per session: another session's turns never evict a session's mapping, a session's own oldest mappings are evicted only beyond its own bound, and a late end whose mapping was evicted changes no row (left to terminal reconciliation); a test covers that eviction.
When a session is removed, its Codex turn mappings are dropped; a test shows none remain for it after removal.
Focused tests covering the change and its new tests pass in the item's named worktree, and the full gate is green on the frozen input.
The review pair (Codex and Claude, read-only) has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding on the frozen input.
